reason: The sources provide over 15 consistent claims from at least six different websites, covering Haumea's discovery, unique physical properties, and ring system.
story: In the cold reaches of the Kuiper Belt, there is a dwarf planet that defies the typical roundness of space. Haumea is the fastest-spinning large object in our solar system, completing a full rotation in just 3.9 hours. This extreme speed generates massive centrifugal force, stretching the rocky world into a triaxial ellipsoid—essentially the shape of a giant cosmic egg or football. Discovered amid a bitter scientific dispute between American and Spanish teams, Haumea was eventually named after the Hawaiian goddess of childbirth. Its violent past is evident; an ancient catastrophic collision likely stripped away its outer layers and created its two moons, Hi'iaka and Namaka. In 2017, astronomers discovered that Haumea also possesses its own ring system—the first ever found beyond Neptune. Coated in bright crystalline water ice and marked by a mysterious dark red spot, Haumea is a spinning relic of the early solar system's chaos.
angle: Haumea spins so fast—once every 3.9 hours—that it has physically deformed into the shape of a giant egg and sprouted its own ring system.

claims.claim: Haumea was discovered in 2004 and announced in 2005.
Haumea is the fastest-spinning large object in the solar system.
The dwarf planet completes one rotation every 3.9 hours.
Rapid rotation has distorted Haumea into a triaxial ellipsoid or egg shape.
Haumea possesses a ring system, discovered in 2017.
The ring was discovered by observing a stellar occultation.
The ring is approximately 70 kilometers wide.
Haumea has two known moons named Hi'iaka and Namaka.
The dwarf planet is named after the Hawaiian goddess of fertility and childbirth.
Haumea is located in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune's orbit.
The Caltech discovery team used the nickname 'Santa' for the object.
Haumea's surface is coated in crystalline water ice.
There is a dark red spot on Haumea's surface that is richer in minerals and organic compounds.
Haumea is the largest member of a collisional family sharing similar orbits and composition.
Haumea's orbital period around the Sun is approximately 283 to 285 years.
The dwarf planet's extreme spin was likely caused by a giant ancient collision.

disputed: Discovery credit is disputed between Mike Brown's Caltech team and Jose Luis Ortiz's Spanish team; the script should note that both claim discovery in different years (2003 vs 2004).

Haumea's status in hydrostatic equilibrium is debated, with some recent models casting doubt while others cite it as a perfect example; the script should attribute this to 'recent mathematical models'.
Size ranking varies, with some sources calling it the third largest TNO and others the fourth largest dwarf planet; the script should say 'one of the largest'.
Density estimates vary significantly from 1.8 g/cm3 to 2.6 g/cm3 based on different modeling techniques; the script should use general terms like 'rocky interior'.
